info.title: host/authority/v1/authority.proto
info.description:
The authority interface: what a module or solution calls on its host to be
issued a Work Context, to have one checked, and to learn the keys it was
signed with, and to ask which resources of a kind it covers. Every former spelling (start task, start
installation task, exchange audience, start child, renew, the module broker's
mints) is Issue with a different `as`.

post.summary:
Check verifies a presented Work Context for the audience the caller is,
re-checking the authorization revision and the seal live.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: CheckRequest presents a capability for verification.

post.summary:
Issue signs a Work Context for one owner shape, one audience and the scopes
asked for, bounded by what the owner holds and what the audience declared.
Served over REST too (POST /v1/authority:issue), for a module with no
generated client of its own, as a Python service: the same request and
answer, in JSON.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: IssueRequest names on whose behalf the capability is issued.

audience.description: The audience the caller is; a capability addressed elsewhere is refused.

method.description:
The method the capability is presented to: "/package.Service/Method" for a
gRPC call, "<VERB> <path>" for an HTTP request (GET /v1/model/profiles),
matched against the routes the module declares. When set, the check also
applies what the audience module's delivery declares for that method, and
refuses by name a call that does not hold it, a method that declares
nothing, and a method the module does not serve.

advisory.description:
Advisory asks for the policy decision without its refusal: the capability
is still verified and refused when it is not sound, but what the method
declares is only reported, in CheckResponse.refusal, and the verified
capability is answered. A hop in a composition that runs permissive
(hop/ENFORCEMENT=warn) asks this way and logs the refusal it did not make.
Hosts may refuse advisory outside local development runs.

v1CheckRequest.description: CheckRequest presents a capability for verification.

authorizationRevision.description: The owner's authorization revision as of this check.

refusal.description:
Refusal is what the method's policy would have refused, verbatim, when the
check was advisory and the policy did not hold; empty when it held.

delegationId.description: The delegation's id, as Delegate answered it.

v1InstallationRef.description: InstallationRef names an installation acting for itself.

person.description:
The signed-in person making this call, identified by the bearer the call
carries; the host opened that session at sign-in.

workload.description: A module's own workload, proving which module it is.

installation.description:
An installation acting for itself, with the scope the organisation consented to.
actor must authenticate a workload of that installation's solution.

parentToken.description: One more hop from an existing capability: a child, an exchange or a renewal.

delegation.description:
A delegation a person granted the module acting (actor): the capability
is owned by that person and carries the delegation on the module's hop.
No live capability is presented: the authority re-checks the delegation
and what its grantor holds now, so a revoked delegation or a lost role
stops the next issue, and renewing is issuing again.

audience.description: The module principal that may consume the capability.

scopes.description: The scopes asked for; empty means everything the owner holds at the audience.

ttlSeconds.description: Requested lifetime in seconds; clamped to the issuer's ceiling.

operationBindingId.description:
The declared binding this capability exercises, when the owner is a workload
or a child acts through one.

organizationId.description:
The organisation the work runs in. A workload may leave this empty when
exactly one organisation has an active installation of its module.
Otherwise it must name the organisation of the work item;
absent or ambiguous installation authority is refused with a reason.

actor.description:
The acting workload credential; required with parent_token, delegation,
and installation. For installation it must name the installed solution.

operation.description:
Which of the binding's operations the capability is for: "invoke" (the
default for a person, a child or a delegation), "headless" (the default for
a workload) or "lookup": the binding's lookup scopes alone, to read a
receipt without the authority to repeat the effect.

v1IssueRequest.description: IssueRequest names on whose behalf the capability is issued.

token.description: The signed capability, as a caller presents it.

context.description: The decoded capability, for the holder to read its own claims.

v1IssueResponse.description: IssueResponse carries the signed capability and its decoded form.

v1PersonSession.description:
PersonSession names the caller's own session. It carries no field: the person
is whoever the bearer on the call authenticates as, so a caller cannot ask for
another person's authority by naming a session.

principalId.description: principal_id identifies the actor this hop delegated to.

principalKind.description:
principal_kind distinguishes the sort of principal, so a human and an
agent bearing the same id are not conflated.

delegationId.description:
delegation_id identifies the delegation that produced this hop, so the
chain stays auditable back to its grant.

grantedScopes.description:
granted_scopes are this actor's effective scopes, a subset of the
preceding hop's.

agentId.description:
agent_id is the actor's agent manifest identity. Required when
principal_kind is "agent" and absent otherwise.

organizationId.description:
organization_id is the organization this actor belongs to, when it is not
the one the task runs in. An org-bridge agent acts in an organization the
owner does not belong to, and authorization is scoped to the actor's own.

principalEpoch.description:
principal_epoch is THIS actor's epoch, distinct from the owner's epoch in
the seal. Advancing it invalidates every capability in which this
principal is an actor, without touching the owner's.

It exists because the seal's epoch is the task owner's, and an actor's
authority can be narrowed independently of the owner's: a delegated
operation context may have a person as its owner and a service principal
as its actor, and narrowing that service principal must reach the
capabilities it acts in. Without this field the only lever for a
compromised actor is the tenant's authorization_revision, which cuts off
every capability of the tenant.

REQUIRED, for the reason seal gives. A hop with no epoch is a principal
nothing can revoke, and leaving that expressible on the wire made it a
shape a consumer could mint without noticing.

v1WorkActorV1.description:
WorkActorV1 is one verified delegated actor. granted_scopes are the actor's
effective scopes and must monotonically attenuate the previous hop.

principalKind.description: principal_kind distinguishes the sort of principal the approver is.

v1WorkApproverV1.description:
WorkApproverV1 is one principal whose decision produced a grant. It carries
the kind as well as the id: a policy that requires a human approver cannot
be written against bare identifiers.

keyId.description: key_id selects one public verification key during rotation.

issuer.description: issuer is the authority that verified identity and minted this context.

audience.description: audience is the exact service or trust boundary allowed to consume it.

notBeforeUnix.description:
not_before_unix is the earliest instant a verifier may accept this
capability.

issuedAtUnix.description: issued_at_unix is when the issuer minted it.

expiresAtUnix.description:
expires_at_unix is the instant it stops being accepted. Exchanging a
parent capability for a child one never extends it.

nonce.description: nonce identifies the capability. Replay behavior is separately explicit.

authorizationRevision.description: authorization_revision is the issuer's current membership/policy revision.

replayPolicy.description:
replay_policy is "idempotent" or "single-use". A verifier still needs a
durable replay store to enforce single-use consumption.

tenantId.description:
tenant_id is the first element of the task identity tuple and is carried
unchanged across every hop.

ownerPrincipalId.description:
owner_principal_id is the principal on whose authority the task runs. It
is the delegating owner, not necessarily the current actor.

taskId.description: task_id completes the task identity tuple and survives child agents.

sessionId.description:
session_id identifies this hop. Starting a child agent mints a new one
rather than mutating this capability.

parentSessionId.description:
parent_session_id is the session this one was exchanged from; absent on
the first session of a task.

authorityScopes.description:
authority_scopes are the maximum scopes the owner delegated into this
Work Context. Each actor hop's granted_scopes must be a subset of the
preceding effective scopes.

actorChain.description:
actor_chain is ordered from the first delegated actor to the current actor.
The owner is not duplicated here merely to make a direct call look uniform.
Every hop attenuates the one before it, except the final hop of a
capability carrying grant_hop.

attributionTeamIds.description:
attribution_team_ids is an immutable verified attribution snapshot. It
explains ownership; current authorization is still evaluated separately.

workspaceId.description:
workspace_id is the workspace the task runs against, when the task is
scoped to one.

projectId.description:
project_id narrows workspace_id to a single project, when the task is
scoped that far.

ownerPrincipalKind.description:
owner_principal_kind distinguishes the sort of principal the owner is, so
a verifier can present the owner without resolving it against a directory.
Optional on the wire: a capability minted before this field existed is
still a valid capability, and an archived receipt embedding one still
verifies. Deriving an identity from a capability that omits it is the
error, raised where the identity is built.

ownerAgentId.description:
owner_agent_id is the owner's agent manifest identity. Required when
owner_principal_kind is "agent" and absent otherwise.

organizationId.description:
organization_id is the organization the task runs in. It is not the
tenant: a tenant may hold several organizations, and authorization is
scoped per organization. An actor hop may name a different one.

grantHop.description:
grant_hop is the approval grant this capability was minted under. It is
the one audited exception to the attenuation rule: the final actor hop
holds exactly granted_scope, which the preceding hop need not contain.
Present only on a single-use child capability minted for one approved
call; absent on every ordinary session.

seal.description:
seal binds this capability to one installation and one execution: the
principal's epoch, the installation and revision it was minted for, and
the build incarnation it was minted on. A verifier compares every field
against the live value and refuses on any mismatch, which is what stops a
capability outliving the installation or the build it was issued against.

REQUIRED. An earlier version of this field was optional, with the stated
reason that a schema rule would invalidate every archived capability and
every receipt embedding one, so the requirement belonged in the verifier.
Two independent reviews named that for what it is: a backward-compatibility
hedge, which the rules in force forbid. It also meant every reader other
than the verifier saw a capability's binding to its installation as
optional, so the strongest check in the model was the easiest one for a
consumer to not notice.

Archived capabilities and receipts are historical DATA. If they must be
read after this, they get a snapshot type of their own rather than keeping
the live credential permanently weaker than it should be.

operationBinding.description:
operation_binding is the unit of authority this capability exercises,
sealed by its id, revision and incarnation. Present on an operation
context and absent on a session that exercises none.

The id is what a verifier looks the binding up by, exactly. Nothing
searches the bindings for one that contains the capability's scopes: a
search is a predicate someone wrote, and a predicate one case too
generous grants authority nobody reviewed.

v1WorkContextV1.description:
WorkContextV1 is the product-neutral identity and authority capability for
one Task/Session hop. The signed wire representation is owned by Codefly
SDKs; applications must never serialize this message into a bearer token or
construct the transport header themselves.

Task identity is the tuple (tenant_id, owner_principal_id, task_id).
Starting a child agent keeps that tuple and exchanges the parent capability
for a new child session capability. It never mutates an existing capability.

grantId.description:
grant_id identifies the approval grant, so revoking the grant and
auditing the call both reach the same record.

approvers.description:
approvers are the principals whose decision produced the grant, every one
of an N-of-M quorum, so the audit record is complete.

grantedScope.description:
granted_scope is exactly what the approval added: one resource_kind, one
action and one resource_id. A grant never widens beyond that triple.

subject.description:
subject is what the grant is pinned to, in the approvals engine's own
vocabulary, so a grant approved for one subject cannot be spent on another.

requestDigest.description: request_digest binds the grant to the exact call the approver saw.

v1WorkGrantHopV1.description:
WorkGrantHopV1 records the approval that justifies a capability holding
authority its delegating owner never held. It is minted only as a new child
capability bound to one tool, one subject and one call, so the authority it
adds is unusable anywhere else and expires with the grant window.

bindingId.description:
binding_id is the host's identifier for the binding. The verifier looks it
up EXACTLY: nothing searches the bindings for one that fits a capability's
scopes, because a search is a predicate somebody wrote and a predicate one
case too generous grants authority nobody reviewed.

This comment used to say the id "is never derived from the binding's
contents, because a derived id is one a caller can compute for a binding
it was never granted". I refuted a review finding against that sentence by
reading it in isolation and judging it correct. The reviewer was right and
I was wrong: solutionhost/authority.go says the opposite in the package
that owns the id — deriving it deterministically is delivery's business
and better than random, and "predictability costs nothing here: an id is
neither a secret nor a capability".

Predictability costs nothing because ENTITLEMENT is what refuses a binding
a caller does not hold, not obscurity: the verifier requires the resolved
binding to be granted to the exercising principal within the installation
the capability is sealed to. Guessing an id gets you a refusal. Resting
the rule on unguessability was the retracted reasoning, and leaving it
here contradicted the package it describes.

revision.description:
revision is the binding's revision at mint time. A verifier holding a
different revision refuses.

incarnation.description:
incarnation is the binding's incarnation at mint time, which changes when
the binding is re-established rather than merely revised.

v1WorkOperationBindingV1.description:
WorkOperationBindingV1 is the unit of authority an operation context
exercises, sealed so that a verifier resolves exactly one binding and
compares it rather than deciding which binding the capability's scopes fit.

resourceKind.description: resource_kind is the class of resource the scope grants against.

actions.description: actions are the operations permitted on that kind.

resourceIds.description:
resource_ids narrows the scope to specific resources. Empty means every
resource of resource_kind.

resourceOwnerId.description:
resource_owner_id narrows the scope to the resources this principal owns
(an installed solution's principal). Empty means the scope selects no
owner. With resource_ids, a resource is covered only when both match. A
reader that cannot compare a resource's owner must not treat an
owner-selected scope as covering the whole kind. It is at most 512 bytes
of printable ASCII other than space and "*" (0x21-0x29, 0x2B-0x7E): no
whitespace, control, non-ASCII, invisible or lookalike character, so two
owners that print alike are the same bytes and every regex engine answers
the rule the same way.

v1WorkScopeV1.description:
WorkScopeV1 is a structured, product-neutral capability scope. Empty
resource_ids means every resource of resource_kind; a child may narrow that
wildcard to explicit IDs but may never widen an explicit parent set.

principalEpoch.description:
principal_epoch is the principal's current epoch. Advancing it
invalidates every capability minted for that principal, which is how a
compromised principal is cut off without waiting for expiry.

installationId.description:
installation_id identifies one organization's installation of one module.
Authority is held through an installation, so a capability that names none
is bound to nothing.

installationRevision.description:
installation_revision is the installation's revision at mint time. A
verifier holding a different revision refuses: the scope of an
installation changes with its revision, so a capability sealed to an
earlier one asks for authority under terms that no longer apply.

v1WorkSealV1.description:
WorkSealV1 binds a capability to one installation and one execution. Its
principal_epoch is the TASK OWNER'S; an actor hop carries its own in
WorkActorV1.principal_epoch, because an actor's authority is narrowed
independently of the owner's. Every
field is a value the issuer holds live and the verifier compares exactly, so
a capability minted before an installation was revised, a principal's
authority was reset, or a build was replaced stops verifying at that moment
rather than at its own expiry.

credential.description: The launcher-signed credential, as core's native issuer writes it.

v1WorkloadCredential.description:
WorkloadCredential proves which module a running process is: the native
launcher credential core's workloadidentity defines, signed by the one launcher
the host was handed an anchor for.
